title: Swap the hotend on a Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D printer: buckle open, old hotend to its holder, new one seated, locked
instruction: Change the 3D printer's hotend: unlock the buckle and swing it open, take the old hotend out and stand it in the empty slot of the holder, then put the new hotend in until it sits flush and lock the buckle.
context: Robot building: low-cost robot arms are built from printed parts (LeRobot's SO-ARM100 printing guide lists Bambu Lab A/P/X-series printers; XLeRobot's parts were printed on a Bambu Lab A1), so a lab building them keeps its printers running as part of the build. Between parts the hotend is swapped to clear a clog, replace a worn nozzle or change size for the next part (0.2 mm for fine detail, hardened steel for abrasive carbon-fibre filament). Bambu's procedure for the A1 series (wiki: Hotend Replacement for A1 Series; the A1 mini takes the same hotend): with the printer off and cool, the filament cut and the front cover and silicone sock off, push the nozzle buckle to the right to unlock it and swing its left side out, hold the heatsink and pull the hotend out, put the new one in until it sits flush, close the buckle and lock it. The hard part: a small part taken out and seated under the toolhead, between unlocking and locking.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Bambu Lab A1 mini 3D printer, powered off and cold, front toward the robot; a loose 5.5 kg block model: base 28 x 24 x 7 cm (x 27.5 to 55.5, y -12 to 12) with an 18 x 18 cm bed; Z column at the right rear; X arm and carriage behind the toolhead. Toolhead (front cover and silicone sock off, filament cut) parked with the hotend's axis at x 37.5, y 0, its part-cooling ducts' undersides 20 cm up. Installed hotend (0.4 mm, dark heatsink) as on the A1: heatsink 2 cm front to back, 1.55 cm wide, 1.65 cm tall, in a recess under the toolhead's body with its front 0.85 cm proud of the body, resting on the heating assembly (22.46 cm up) with its magnet block against the assembly's mounting plate; 0.65 cm tube in the assembly's groove; nozzle 0.35 cm below the ducts. Buckle: a 1.5 cm bar across the front of the tube, 1.55 to 1.85 cm below the heatsink, on a vertical hinge at its right end that rides a 0.25 cm slide; locked, its left end sits behind a catch on the left duct; a 0.8 x 0.5 x 0.5 cm tab on its front near the left end. Hotends: Bambu Hotend - A1 Series, 4.73 cm long, 18 g. Holder: printed PLA, 200 g, loose: a 4 x 16 x 7 cm block (x 23 to 27, y -5 to 11) with two 1.2 x 1 x 3 cm bosses on top (tops 10 cm up), each with a 0.75 cm square hole for the tube: the right slot at y -3.5 holds the new hotend (0.2 mm, green tag, heatsink on the boss), the left one at y 9.5 is empty.
scoring: Score = 0.2 x old out + 0.4 x new seated + 0.3 x locked + 0.1 x finished; 0 if the new hotend is dropped. Old out: the old hotend stands in a holder slot (either; only the left one is free at the start; axis within 0.3 cm of the slot's, heatsink on the boss within 0.3 cm, within 8 degrees of upright) and was not dropped on the way. Dropped: a hotend falls 2 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 1.5 cm of its heatsink while not in the recess or a slot, or its nozzle reaches the bed or the table. New seated: the new hotend within 0.1 cm of its seat along each axis (on the heating assembly, flush against the mounting plate, centred) and within 3 degrees of upright. Locked: with the new hotend seated, the buckle within 4 degrees of shut and its slide within 0.06 cm of the locked end (the bar's left end behind the catch). Finished: seated and locked, no finger pad within 1 cm of the new hotend's heatsink or the buckle, and the new hotend still for 20 steps (1 s); the run is a success, and ends, once that has held with the old hotend in a slot. Real trial, from photos and the video: old out = standing upright in either holder slot (end photo); locked = the buckle shut and pushed back left so that it is latched (end photo; it will not open by pulling its left side); finished = no part of either gripper touches the new hotend or the buckle in the last 1 s (video); seated = the heatsink flush against the toolhead (a strip of printer paper, about 0.1 mm, does not slide between it and the heating assembly) and no wobble when the heatsink is nudged; dropped = the new hotend falls or is set down on the bed, the table or the floor.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the old hotend back in the recess and close and lock the buckle, stand the new hotend in the holder's right slot, and put the printer and the holder back on their tape marks. Real trials: the printer stays off and cool (below 50 C) with the front cover and silicone sock off and the filament cut; powered off, its toolhead slides along the X arm, so slide it back to its tape mark (hotend axis at y 0) before each trial; the two hotends may swap roles between trials.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; printer a loose 5.5 kg block model, toolhead fixed to it. Hotend at the real one's size (47.3 mm, heatsink 20 x 15.5 x 16.5 mm, 18 g); toolhead and duct sizes estimated from photos. No magnet: the hotend rests on the heating assembly and the closed buckle holds it. Buckle: push 2.5 mm right on a damped slide to free its left end from a catch, swing out (a light spring holds it open), shut, push back left to lock; its parts are 20-50 g (real ~5 g) for the solver.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps; both arms stayed in front of the printer and neither reached the toolhead); demo: 1.0 (1,128 steps; scripted, both arms)
